note: One row per result. Status is not editorial. A result that turned out false stays in the table with status 'disproved', because the record of what failed is the point.

legend.proved: Proved on paper, and in some cases machine-checked in Lean.
legend.verified: Established by exact computation over a stated search range. Not a proof.
legend.disproved: A claim that was believed, tested, and found false. Includes my own.
legend.scooped: Correct, but already in the literature. Found during a novelty check.

results.statement: Closed the main open step behind one direction of a 2020 result on quadratic irrationals (Example 6.4), though the governing principle behind the closing argument was already partially present in the published literature; the composite argument and its consequence for the mismatch ratio are the new part.
results.plain: Closed the open half of a 2020 quadratic-irrationals theorem (Example 6.4); the closing argument and its mismatch-ratio consequence are new.

results.statement: For any nonsquare d, the quantity [sqrt d]_q + [-sqrt d]_q equals (A-D)/C read off the fundamental Pell automorph, reducing an infinite question to one divisibility check.
results.plain: Proved [sqrt d]_q + [-sqrt d]_q = (A-D)/C from the fundamental Pell automorph, turning an infinite search into one divisibility check.

results.statement: Theorem A: the vanishing locus is the torsion of a fixed hypersurface in a torus, which turns an observed pattern into a theorem by way of Laurent's theorem (Invent. Math. 78, 1984).
results.plain: Proved the vanishing locus is the torsion of a fixed hypersurface in a torus (Theorem A), via Laurent's theorem.

results.statement: Downward closure: for l in {2,3,4,5}, any prime p and any a >= 1, Phi_{p^a l} dividing S forces Phi_l to divide S, at every word length.
results.plain: Proved downward closure: Phi_{p^a l} dividing S forces Phi_l to divide S, for l in {2,3,4,5}, at every word length.

results.statement: The scalar congruence conjecture is settled by the exact identity q(A-D) = (q-1)(qB+C).
results.plain: Settled the scalar congruence conjecture with the exact identity q(A-D) = (q-1)(qB+C).

results.statement: Lemma N gives negation closure at all lengths, not only the lengths that were checked by hand.
results.plain: Proved negation closure (Lemma N) at all lengths, not only the lengths checked by hand.

results.statement: Every word in the length-5 list vanishes for all k: five parametrised shapes plus ten identically zero words.
results.plain: Proved every word in the length-5 list vanishes for all k: five parametrised shapes plus ten identically zero words.

results.statement: That the length-5 list is complete, so no other word vanishes, is verified for 4 <= k <= 24 and is not proved.
results.plain: Verified the length-5 list is complete (no other word vanishes) for 4 <= k <= 24; not proved for all k.

results.statement: The degree equality clause is proved by a continuant tightness induction.
results.plain: Proved the degree-equality clause by a continuant tightness induction.

results.statement: Lemma L at odd prime powers follows from downward closure (DC) alone, by a pi-adic argument.
results.plain: Proved Lemma L at odd prime powers from downward closure alone, by a p-adic argument.

results.statement: The intertwining relation NMN = M^-1 holds exactly when x = b0 sqrt(D) with b0 rational, which is a strictly larger family than the pure square roots the manuscript hypothesis assumed.
results.plain: Proved NMN = M^-1 holds for the strictly wider family x = b0 sqrt(D), b0 rational, not just the pure square roots the manuscript assumed.

results.statement: In a tested panel of cubic irrationals (heptagon, nonagon and S_3 cubics), the negation sum and product are not finite, checked exactly to N = 320. No proof for all cubics is written.
results.plain: Checked a panel of cubic irrationals: none gives a finite negation sum or product, exact to N = 320. Not proved for all cubics.

results.statement: [x+y]_q is not a bihomographic function of [x]_q and [y]_q over Q(q): the 8-wide relation matrix has full rank 8, so the kernel is trivial.
results.plain: Proved [x+y]_q is not bihomographic in [x]_q and [y]_q over Q(q): the 8-wide relation matrix has full rank 8.

results.statement: [xy]_q is likewise not bihomographic, and unlike the addition case the q-reversal is absent as the obstruction.
results.plain: Proved [xy]_q is likewise not bihomographic, with the q-reversal obstruction absent this time.

results.statement: First q-real modular law proved end to end by Christol's theorem plus the Walnut automatic-theorem prover: n congruent to 1 mod 3 implies c_n is even.
results.plain: Proved a q-real modular law end to end with Christol's theorem plus the Walnut automatic prover: n = 1 mod 3 implies c_n is even.

results.statement: The biconditional version of the same statement is false, with 4446 counterexamples in range.
results.plain: Disproved the biconditional version of the same law: 4,446 counterexamples in range.

results.statement: The claim that the negation sum is finite exactly for trace-zero quadratics is false. Counterexamples: sqrt(19), sqrt(43), sqrt(46), sqrt(53), all trace zero with infinite sum.
results.plain: Disproved my own trace-zero finiteness criterion; counterexamples sqrt(19), sqrt(43), sqrt(46), sqrt(53).

results.statement: The beta tail-degree bound is false. Canonical counterexample x = -16 + (48/7) sqrt 3, confirmed by three independent attempts.
results.plain: Disproved the beta tail-degree bound; counterexample x = -16 + (48/7)sqrt(3), confirmed by three independent implementations.

results.statement: The manuscript partition claim is false. Smallest counterexample d = 60, a = 11, where S = Phi2 Phi3 Phi4 Phi5 Phi6 admits no valid partition.
results.plain: Disproved the manuscript's partition claim; smallest counterexample d = 60, a = 11.

results.statement: The vanishing-sums-of-roots-of-unity route (Mann, Conway-Jones, Lam-Leung) does not prove the length-5 classification. The weight condition is satisfied trivially, so the argument is vacuous.
results.plain: Showed the vanishing-sums-of-roots-of-unity route cannot prove the length-5 classification; the weight condition holds trivially, so the argument is vacuous.

results.statement: The rival count-law formula 2(4^m - 1)/3 predicts 170 at length 9. The observed value is 168, which refutes it. Leading coefficients are Catalan numbers at even lengths.
results.plain: Refuted the rival count-law formula 2(4^m-1)/3: it predicts 170 at length 9, the true value is 168.

results.statement: The nine hand-derived length-5 cases are each individually correct but the list is not complete. Missing families appear at every k >= 3.
results.plain: Found the nine hand-derived length-5 cases individually correct but incomplete; missing families appear at every k >= 3.

results.statement: The off-axis census result of 100.0000 percent with zero exceptions was a window-floor bug, not an effect. The corrected run gives 97.36 percent with 15929 exceptions.
results.plain: Traced a 100.0000 percent, zero-exception census result to a window-floor bug; corrected figure is 97.36 percent with 15,929 exceptions.
results.latex: \underbrace{100.0000\%,\ 0\ \text{exceptions}}_{\text{window-floor bug}}\ \longrightarrow\ \underbrace{97.36\%,\ 15929\ \text{exceptions}}_{\text{corrected}}

results.statement: A pilot disagreement was misdiagnosed as a truncation artifact. The real cause was a floating-point deduplication bug that treated sqrt(6) and sqrt(2) times sqrt(3) as distinct catalog entries.
results.plain: Traced a misdiagnosed pilot disagreement to a floating-point bug treating sqrt(6) and sqrt(2)*sqrt(3) as distinct catalog entries.

results.statement: The rational jump gap has the universal closed form (1-q) q^E / (S+ S-). Derived independently, then found published: Etingof arXiv:2508.08440 Proposition 4.11 in continuant form, and Jouteur, Paris-Romaskevich and Thomas arXiv:2603.04295v2 Proposition 3.22 in this closed form.
results.plain: Derived the closed form (1-q)q^E/(S+S-) for the rational jump gap independently, then found it published (Etingof arXiv:2508.08440; Jouteur, Paris-Romaskevich and Thomas arXiv:2603.04295v2).

results.statement: The S'(1) formula 2S'(1) = d deg S + a^-1 - a is already known: Lasker, arXiv:2309.10819, Lemma 6.1 and Corollary 6.2.
results.plain: Derived 2S'(1) = d deg S + a^-1 - a independently; already known (Lasker, arXiv:2309.10819, Lemma 6.1 and Corollary 6.2).

results.statement: The level-six claim that Phi6 dividing S_i forces [6]_q to divide S_i is Byakuno-Ren-Yanagawa, arXiv:2603.08439, Proposition 5.3. Only the A_i profile in that write-up is new.
results.plain: Proved the level-six divisibility claim independently; matches Byakuno-Ren-Yanagawa arXiv:2603.08439 Proposition 5.3, with the A_i profile as the new part.
results.latex: i\ge1,\ c_1,\dots,c_i\in\mathbb{Z}:\qquad \Phi_6\mid S_i\ \Longrightarrow\ [6]_q\mid S_i,\quad\text{hence }6\mid S_i(1)

results.statement: Among all 668745 canonical quadratic irrationals in (1,2) with D <= 20000 and height <= 10, the negation sum is finite for exactly two constants: sqrt(2) and sqrt(3).
results.plain: Swept 668,745 canonical quadratic irrationals; the negation sum is finite for exactly two, sqrt(2) and sqrt(3).

results.statement: For x = m/(m^2 - 1), the reduced q-denominator collapses to exactly two cyclotomic factors precisely when m-1 and m+1 are twin primes.
results.plain: Proved the reduced q-denominator of m/(m^2-1) collapses to two cyclotomic factors exactly when m-1 and m+1 are twin primes.

results.statement: The realizability index-set law, stated as connectivity closure minus the n with 4 | n and n not a power of 2, matches 166 of 166 census cases exactly. The proof is open.
results.plain: The realizability index-set law matches 166 of 166 census cases exactly; recorded as unproved, since the proof is still open.

results.statement: The k-independence of the vanishing-locus congruence conditions is confirmed exactly for k = 2 through 13.
results.plain: Confirmed k-independence of the vanishing-locus congruence conditions for k = 2 through 13.

results.statement: All 49 integer pairs (a,b) in {-3..3}^2 for the q-twisted Somos-4 recurrence stay Laurent through x_4 to x_11, and 48 of the 49 are not trivial reparametrisations.
results.plain: Checked all 49 integer pairs for the q-twisted Somos-4 recurrence stay Laurent through x_4 to x_11; 48 of 49 are non-trivial reparametrisations.

results.statement: The heptagon and nonagon cyclic cubics recover the Ovsienko-Ustinov degree-3 functional equation exactly, with residual zero to q^4950. Non-cyclic S_3 cubics admit no such equation.
results.plain: Recovered the Ovsienko-Ustinov degree-3 functional equation from the heptagon and nonagon cyclic cubics, residual zero to q^4950.

results.statement: The divisor hypothesis is a theorem for n <= 6, by Kogiso-Miyamoto-Ren-Wakui-Yanagawa and Byakuno-Ren-Yanagawa. For n >= 7 it is open.
results.plain: The divisor hypothesis holds for n <= 6 (Kogiso-Miyamoto-Ren-Wakui-Yanagawa; Byakuno-Ren-Yanagawa); open for n >= 7.

results.statement: The true criterion for finiteness of the negation sum is a continued-fraction period condition, and it remains open. The palindrome-period argument fails at d = 19, whose period is palindromic.
results.plain: The finiteness criterion for the negation sum is still open; the palindrome-period argument fails at d = 19.
